_comment: The baseline WER ledger for egs/yesno/asr.
reference_wer is the number in egs/yesno/asr/README.md, measured by the
author on CUDA with torch 2.1. measured_wer is what this repository
produces now, recorded from the run named under `measured`. max_wer is
the gate.
**Re-anchored to the Python pipeline.** Every number under
measured_wer was previously from run 44962562909, taken on
83-dimensional features with Kaldi doing the data preparation, the
language directory, the features and CMVN. None of that is true any
more: yesno trains with no Kaldi at all. So the measurements are from
run 46155782177, which is the first run of the pipeline as it now is,
and `features.measured_at` finally equals `features.current`.
**max_wer was not touched when re-anchoring**, and that is deliberate.
It is measured_wer-plus-three-errors against the *old* measurement, so
some gates now sit a little wider relative to their topology and some a
little narrower. Tightening them wants more than two runs: the spread
between the last Kaldi-pipeline run and this one is one word error in
1,856 across eight topologies, moving in both directions, which is the
whole evidence available about run-to-run variation on this corpus.
A third and fourth run would make a real band; two runs would make a
guess that happened to be written down.
test_yesno has 232 reference words, so one word error is 0.43%. That is
the resolution limit of this corpus: it cannot distinguish a change
worth less than one error, which is why mini-librispeech exists.
Judge a change against measured_wer. **Raising max_wer to make a run
pass is how a ledger stops meaning anything** -- if a run exceeds the
gate, find out why.
utterances pins the data split. It is 31/29 rather than an even 30/30
because that is the split the published results were measured on: it
arose from two README files in the corpus being counted as waves, and
local/prepare_data.py now states the count explicitly so that filtering
them out did not move an utterance across. 29 test utterances of eight
words each is the 232 above.
reference_wer remains an 83-dimensional CUDA measurement and is not
re-anchored: it is the historical record, and the comparison against it
is what showed that dropping pitch cost three word errors in total.

features.note: The two agree for the first time since pitch was dropped: these numbers were measured on the features the recipe computes now, by run/make_fbank.py rather than steps/make_fbank.sh, written compressed so the archive is on the same 8-bit grid Kaldi's was. See CLAUDE.md on why pitch went.

measured.note: The first yesno run whose data preparation, language directory, features, CMVN and topologies were all Python: no Kaldi binary or script touches anything these numbers depend on. CPU, torch 2.15, --dither=0. reference_wer is still the author's pre-refactor CUDA run at torch 2.1, kept as the historical record.

previous.note: The last run before the preparation became Python, on ff0088f, three hours earlier and on a different image build. Its errors were 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2 for the topologies in this file's order against this run's 1, 1, 1, 0, 2, 0, 2, 2 -- eight becoming nine, moving in both directions. That is the run-to-run spread of training on this corpus, not a pipeline difference, and it is why re-anchoring was recorded rather than treated as a regression.
